# vktSynchronizationInternallySynchronizedTests

## Overview

`vktSynchronizationInternallySynchronizedTests.cpp` tests concurrent access to one Vulkan queue created with `VK_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INTERNALLY_SYNCHRONIZED_BIT_KHR`. Four threads submit work without an application-side queue mutex, exercising image draws and several other submission paths at the same time.

This is a **synchronization2-only** and **non-SC** family. It is registered as `synchronization2.internally_synchronized_queues`; it is not the legacy `synchronization` tree's `internally_synchronized_objects` family.

## Registration

The synchronization2 registration is in [`vktSynchronizationTests.cpp`](../../../modules/vulkan/synchronization/vktSynchronizationTests.cpp#L124-L132), where `createInternallySynchronizedTests()` is added only for the synchronization2 group and only outside Vulkan SC builds. The factory's `SynchronizationType` parameter is not used to select a legacy path.

The default [`synchronization2` mustpass file](../../../mustpass/main/vk-default/synchronization2.txt) contains 183 paths under `dEQP-VK.synchronization2.internally_synchronized_queues`.

```text
synchronization2
└── internally_synchronized_queues
    ├── <type3>_<type4>                         # no WSI
    └── <wsi>_<type3>_<type4>                   # WSI involved
```

The mustpass has 49 non-WSI cases and 134 WSI cases. These are registered names; runtime support checks may skip a case when the required extension, feature, queue, or platform is unavailable.

## Case generation and names

Every case fixes threads 1 and 2 to `small` and `large` image draws using the legacy submit path. Threads 3 and 4 are chosen independently from:

| Name | Operation |
|---|---|
| `small2` | Small image draw using `queueSubmit2` |
| `large2` | Large image draw using `queueSubmit2` |
| `bind_sparse` | Sparse buffer/image binding and copy |
| `wsi` | Swapchain acquire, draw, and present |
| `debug_utils` | Draw enclosed by debug-utils queue labels |
| `performance_configuration` | INTEL performance configuration and query operations |
| `out_of_band` | NV low-latency out-of-band queue notification plus draw |
| `device_wait_idle` | Buffer copy combined with `deviceWaitIdle` |

Without WSI, a case is named `<type3>_<type4>`, such as `bind_sparse_debug_utils`. When WSI is involved, a WSI platform prefix is added: `<wsi>_<type3>_<type4>`, such as `headless_wsi_small2` or `xcb_bind_sparse_wsi`. WSI variants use the supported WSI types generated by the source. The Android double-WSI combination is skipped because Android does not support multiple concurrent WSI windows.

## Execution model

For each generated parameter set, the test creates a custom device because the default context device does not have the required queue-creation flags. It enables `VK_KHR_internally_synchronized_queues` and `VK_KHR_synchronization2`, enables the `synchronization2` and `internallySynchronizedQueues` features, and applies conditional extensions/features for the selected operations.

The source varies these queue parameters:

- single queue, first or last internally synchronized queue, and two-queue configurations selecting the first or last internally synchronized queue;
- same or different queue families;
- graphics queues, with sparse-binding support additionally required for sparse cases.

The queue is retrieved with `vkGetDeviceQueue2` and `VK_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INTERNALLY_SYNCHRONIZED_BIT_KHR` in `VkDeviceQueueInfo2`. Four `CaseThread` instances then start and join around the same queue. If two queue families or the requested queue count are unavailable, the source falls back to a single queue where possible; lack of any suitable queue produces a not-supported result.

## Verification

- **Draws (`small`, `large`, `small2`, `large2`)** render a gradient and compare readback pixels against the expected values, allowing a one-byte-per-channel tolerance.
- **Debug-utils** and **out-of-band** cases perform the draw check after adding their respective queue operations.
- **Sparse** cases copy from sparse resources and validate the expected buffer/image contents.
- **WSI**, **performance configuration**, and **device wait idle** cases require their Vulkan operations to complete successfully; WSI uses acquire/draw/present.
- Each worker records operation/check failure; the test joins all workers before returning. (The current `iterate()` implementation does not inspect `CaseThread::hasFailed()` after joining, so recorded draw/check failures are not currently propagated to the test result.)

## Support requirements

All cases require:

- `VK_KHR_internally_synchronized_queues`;
- `VK_KHR_synchronization2`, including the synchronization2 and internally synchronized queues features.

Additional requirements are conditional:

| Case component | Requirement |
|---|---|
| WSI | Platform surface extension, WSI display/window support, and `VK_KHR_swapchain` |
| `debug_utils` | `VK_EXT_debug_utils` |
| `bind_sparse` | Sparse binding and sparse residency image 2D core features |
| `performance_configuration` | `VK_INTEL_performance_query` |
| `out_of_band` | `VK_NV_low_latency2` |
